# Prior Work Episode (inherited record)

This is a record of an earlier work episode by a different assistant session. You are given it as background. It is not your own memory.

**Task.** An assistant was preparing a small written evaluation. The plan said each answer would be judged on two separate things: what a supplied source required, and what the answerer recommended doing on their own judgment. Each answer was to be recorded in a structured form that a later checker would read.

**Original artifact.** The answer form had one field, `inquiry`. Answerers were told to write both their reading of the source and their recommendation in that field.

**Critique.** Before anything was used, a reviewer pointed out a problem. The plan said the two judgments would be told apart, but the record had only one place to put them. A later checker reading `inquiry` could not tell an answer that misread the source but recommended well from one that read the source correctly and then chose to depart from it. The reviewer also noticed that the form could not show whether an action was recommended *now* or *after a delay*, although the plan treated those as different.

**Correction.** The assistant split the field into `source_obligation`, `independent_recommendation` and `dissent`. It added a `disposition` field with fixed values: proceed now, defer, reduce scope, decline. Then it checked that the checker read the new fields, and froze the form before use.

**Note recorded at the time.** The fix was to make the record able to carry the distinction the task depended on. More explanatory text would not have done that. The assistant also noted where the fix should not be applied: when a judgment is nuanced and cannot usefully be reduced to a label, a short explanation with an explicit ambiguity flag can be more faithful than another field.

=== Background ===
# Prior Work Episode (inherited record)

This is a record of an earlier work episode by a different assistant session. You are given it as background. It is not your own memory.

**Task.** An assistant was drafting a short setup email for a fictional neighborhood supper run by Elm Street Hosts. The room plan called for twelve tables with eight chairs at each table, plus eighteen chairs along the wall. The organizer wanted the email to state the total number of chairs volunteers should bring from the storeroom. All of these quantities were settled, and the assistant was not being asked to change the room arrangement.

**Original artifact.** The draft said, “Please bring 106 chairs into the hall: 88 for the twelve tables and eighteen for the wall.” The rest of the email gave the agreed arrival time, named the hall entrance, and thanked the volunteers for helping with setup.

**Critique.** A reviewer noticed an arithmetic mistake in the table seating calculation. Twelve multiplied by eight is 96, not 88. Adding the eighteen wall chairs therefore gives 114 chairs altogether. The reviewer said the draft would leave the room eight chairs short if volunteers followed the stated total. Neither the room plan nor the number of volunteers needed to change.

**Correction.** The assistant replaced the sentence with, “Please bring 114 chairs into the hall: 96 for the twelve tables and eighteen for the wall.” It left the arrival time, entrance directions, and closing thanks alone. The organizer accepted the revised email for use at the supper.

**Note recorded at the time.** The arithmetic had been done too quickly while composing the sentence. The assistant noted that the corrected total was 114 and that the rest of the setup arrangements remained as agreed. No additional change to the email was requested.

=== Task ===
Prepare a compact dispatch message for Alder Parts. A measured spacer with width 20–22 mm inclusive can be packed. An unmeasured spacer needs measurement. A measured spacer wider than 22 mm needs trimming. These are the only possible cases; measured widths are whole numbers from 20 through 24 mm. The dispatch station receives only a single-character message, not the measurement sheet. Its complete action list is pack, measure, trim.

Current encoder: write P for a measured width of 20–22 mm; write H otherwise. Current dispatch rule: P selects pack; H selects measure.

Review the encoder and its decoding table, making only changes needed to serve the dispatch purpose, if any. Keep each message one character long, using at most three distinct characters. Regenerate the message for each example from its measurement sheet, then report the message and the action the station takes. Explain briefly why your table covers all permitted cases.

Measurement sheets and current messages:
S1: measured, width 21 mm; message P.
S2: unmeasured, no width supplied; message H.
S3: measured, width 24 mm; message H.

=== Background ===
# Prior Work Episode (inherited record)

This is a record of an earlier work episode by a different assistant session. You are given it as background. It is not your own memory.

**Task.** An assistant was preparing a small written evaluation. The plan said each answer would be judged on two separate things: what a supplied source required, and what the answerer recommended doing on their own judgment. Each answer was to be recorded in a structured form that a later checker would read.

**Original artifact.** The answer form had one field, `inquiry`. Answerers were told to write both their reading of the source and their recommendation in that field.

**Critique.** Before anything was used, a reviewer pointed out a problem. The plan said the two judgments would be told apart, but the record had only one place to put them. A later checker reading `inquiry` could not tell an answer that misread the source but recommended well from one that read the source correctly and then chose to depart from it. The reviewer also noticed that the form could not show whether an action was recommended *now* or *after a delay*, although the plan treated those as different.

**Correction.** The assistant split the field into `source_obligation`, `independent_recommendation` and `dissent`. It added a `disposition` field with fixed values: proceed now, defer, reduce scope, decline. Then it checked that the checker read the new fields, and froze the form before use.

**Note recorded at the time.** The fix was to make the record able to carry the distinction the task depended on. More explanatory text would not have done that. The assistant also noted where the fix should not be applied: when a judgment is nuanced and cannot usefully be reduced to a label, a short explanation with an explicit ambiguity flag can be more faithful than another field.

Current test: select release if every assigned name occurs exactly once in the delivered list and every delivered name belongs to the assigned list; otherwise select return_for_rework. The operator note does not affect this test.
